text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers.
- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad has called on Malaysian bankers to be more willing to take risks and avoid becoming mere money-lenders.
- The Education Ministry is having discussions with four foreign universities which are interested in setting up branches here, Deputy Education Minister Fong Chan Onn said.
- Penang-based cable and wire maker Leader Cable Industry Bhd has signed a memorandum of undestanding to build a one billion ringgit 100 megawatt power plant in Xiamen City, China.
- Opposition Spirit of 46 will meet on Thursday to finalise preparations for the party's dissolution and enable its members to join Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's UMNO.
- Feud between leaders of a component party of the ruling National Front hots up, with allegations by opposing factions in the Gerakan party of money politics.

- Singapore's reply that an issue on re-merger with Malaysia should not be allowed to harm relations with Kuala Lumpur is too little, too late, said international affairs bureau chief of the Malaysian Chinese Association, Chor Chee Heung.
- The Malacca government is negotiating a deal with Malaysia Aica Bhd chairman Robert Tan which could result in a reverse takeover of the company and project injections.
